seriesAnalysis.opponentPatterns: All five opponents listed CLEAR as their most frequent action: FootballCore21/22 (95%), ERTT27/30 (90%), Lighting Cloud17/19 (89%), Points Donors37/40 (93%), Tik&Taka41/51 (80%). This is a repeated report pattern, not evidence of a shared tactic or successful clear outcomes. Opponent team means were 17-20ms; their reported FWD5 means were 76-80ms.
seriesAnalysis.tacticalReview: The unchanged team went 5W/0D/0L, scored 8 and conceded 1. It had 33:22 shots and 8:1 on target despite only 41.6% mean possession. Four games had opponent possession above 50%, and we won all four. This sample shows possession was not necessary for wins, but does not establish the effect of the setup. Reported PRESS counts by game were 99, 169, 55, 5 and 32; INTERCEPT reached 244 vs Points Donors; MOVE reached 335 vs Tik&Taka. Both MID3 goals against Lighting Cloud and Points Donors came at 2' or 1'; Tik&Taka match went to sudden death. These observations do not isolate causal strategy.
seriesAnalysis.latencyReview: Own report team means were 2434,1172,1905,456,1079ms; four of five exceeded 1s. Median was1172ms, mean1409.2ms. In the 456ms match we won 2-0 with 244 INTERCEPT and 27 SHOOT; high-latency matches included both wins and, in prior batch18, losses. This makes a causal latency conclusion premature. The <=10ms target is not met; investigate per-invocation timestamps, provider first-byte and timeouts rather than tuning from team averages. Match summaries do not identify whether delay came from model, runtime, network, or queue.
seriesAnalysis.decision: Batch19 is a clean unchanged-baseline 5/5 cohort with 15 points and promotion from rank12 to rank10. Retain the lineup for now. The most useful next controlled investigation is latency decomposition across the five reports and a mapping between report shots, SHOOT commands, and shot outcomes; do not assert the repeated opponent CLEAR pattern explains the wins.

note: Five consecutive real ranked matches were completed with the setup unchanged. No benchmarks, practice games, match IDs, credentials, ARNs, account IDs, or raw states are recorded.
